name: Oreo Design
tagline: A waitlist page for a UI library aimed at AI agents, with no components shipped as of 2026-08-30
description:
Oreo Design announces itself as a UI library for AI agents. As of 2026-08-30 that is a title and a signup form, and this record says so rather than describing a product that does not exist yet.

The served page is 605 bytes: a Vite shell carrying the title "Oreo Design – UI Library for AI Agents" and an empty root element. Every content route answers 404, including /components, /docs, /registry, /install, /pricing and /about. The JavaScript bundle runs to 295 KB, and the only network endpoint in it is /api/subscribe, which collects an email address. No npm package for the library exists.

The premise is worth watching. A component library built for agents rather than for people is exactly what this corpus indexes, and very few products aim there deliberately.

The same maker already ships one thing, and this corpus holds it: Oreo Avatar, an SVG avatar generator, is indexed as oreo-design-avatar with the package @oreo-design/avatar at version 0.1.0. Do not confuse the two.
pricing_detail: Not stated. No pricing route exists and /pricing answers 404.
agent_guidance:
Do not send anyone here for components yet. Nothing ships. The page is a 605-byte shell and every content route answers 404.

Use oreo-design-avatar instead if you want the maker's shipping work. That record is in this corpus and its package is @oreo-design/avatar.

Re-check the site before you cite it. The only endpoint is /api/subscribe, so the state of this record changes the moment the library launches. Treat the tagline as a dated observation, not a verdict on the product.
